item.title: Episode 007: The Most Repressed Archetype
item.description:
Matt pulls a deck he hasn’t touched in over a year — the Deviant Moon Tarot, where the clothing is stitched from photographed 19th-century tombstones and nothing in the deck is more than a little bit unsettling — and turns up the Magician: four arms, four tools, and four shadows foreshadowing behind him. Light and dark, baked into one card. What starts as “why don’t I use this deck more” becomes the realest conversation the show has had about creative fear, the machinery that keeps you compliant, and the shadow you can’t afford to repress.

Jaye Anne frames the Magician as all the potential in the world — the perfect little bubble of a dream before anything’s been embodied — and the double-edged fear of popping it to make it real. Matt takes it structural: people don’t create because they’re terrified of their own creations, of what they could actually do. And the system is built to keep it that way. Enter biofuel tickets — Robert Anton Wilson’s name for money — the arrangement where you exchange labor for the right to survive, and your work only “counts” if it’s funding someone else’s dream. From there it goes into shadow: the deck’s own name (deviant + moon), the myth of a God who is only good, fear as an egregore, and a synchronicity too good to script. No answer, as usual — just something with teeth.

In this episode

* The Deviant Moon deck: tombstone-cloth citizens, crescent-moon heads, “why’d you make this card this way,” and the value of knowing an artist’s process

* The Magician as pure potential — and why the main reason people don’t create is that they’re terrified of what they could actually make

* Biofuel tickets: Robert Anton Wilson, the survival tax, and why work “for your own family” or “just to do it” doesn’t count

* The last authentic piece: the dream as the final living vestige, and the risk of bringing it into a world that might just kick it over

* “Deviant Moon” as a name — the excommunicated one, the dark side of the emotions, a full shadow-work deck

* Divine shadow masculine: read the first five books of the Bible with an open mind; repress a pole and it gets louder; the projection screen

* Polarity in every tool and suit — and why creation needs the contrast (bright color on a black ground, bass under the treble, a night chart)

* Fear as an egregore: Jaye Anne’s near-shot-for-shot Star Trek: Voyager memory, fighting vs. confronting, and who actually holds the power

* The most repressed archetype — the summation

* The Commodore 64 dream, Jeri Ryan / Seven of Nine, and collapsing into imposter syndrome the instant the anima validates you

* Bluey, a stick, and the line with teeth: once you make it, it’s not yours anymore

Lines that landed

* “The Magician is the most repressed archetype. Everybody has access to the Magician, but almost no one believes that they have access.” — Matt

* “We’ve decided that people have to do something for us so that they have the right to survive on the planet.” — Matt

* “I’d rather fund my own dream, not someone else’s dream.” — Matt

* “They’re not mad about that, honey. They’re mad about something else and they don’t even know what it is. This is the projection screen.” — Matt

* “Trying to fight it makes it more powerful. It’s actually when you just walk up and confront it that it becomes small.” — Matt

* “You had to have the dark contrast in order to appreciate that.” — Jaye Anne

* “Once you bring something into the world, it’s no longer yours.” — Jaye Anne / “Ooh. That’s got teeth.” — Matt

Referenced

* Deviant Moon Tarot by Patrick Valenza (US Games) — and the deluxe companion book on the making of each card

* Robert Anton Wilson — “biofuel tickets” as a reframe for money

* The Bible — the first five books; Noah out of the boat

* Star Trek: Voyager — the collective-dream episode where an embodiment of fear grows stronger the more it’s fed (an egregore)

* Jeri Ryan / Seven of Nine — the Borg-to-individual arc across Voyager and Picard; Q; the Borg Queen

* Commodore 64 — the retro-platform game-making scene

* A Wrinkle in Time

* Bluey — the beach episode: Bingo’s stick-bird, and the dad’s line

* Concept: the egregore; Black Moon Lilith in the 12th, Scorpio Venus, a night chart

What we left unresolved

Matt names it himself: “like most episodes, we’re not landing on an answer.” The Bluey close is the open door — you create something and all of a sudden it’s not yours — explicitly teed up as a whole other episode they don’t take here. The hardest form of it (your kids as autonomous beings you can’t control) gets set down, not resolved. What you’re supposed to do with the unavoidable fact that creation leaves your hands the moment it’s real stays deliberately unanswered.

Chapters

0:00 — Cold open: rewiring, integration & “unpolished on purpose”

3:21 — The card: The Magician from the Deviant Moon Tarot

6:58 — Four arms, four shadows: the Magician as pure potential

13:09 — Terrified of your own creation

16:45 — Biofuel tickets: Robert Anton Wilson & the survival tax

22:24 — The last authentic piece: doing it just to do it

27:35 — “Deviant Moon”: the shadow-work deck

34:36 — Divine shadow masculine: the God who isn’t only good

42:56 — Every tool has a shadow — and creation needs the contrast

49:28 — Fear is an egregore: Voyager, confront vs. fight & the most repressed archetype

59:04 — Seven of Nine, the Commodore 64 dream & imposter syndrome

1:06:32 — “It’s no longer yours”: the Bluey close

~1h10 · One moment: Matt dreamed — that same night — that Jeri Ryan played his Commodore 64 game and praised it, and he immediately started apologizing for it. The most Magician thing possible, undone the second the anima said “this is good.”

item.title: Episode 006: The Tension Is the Point
item.description:
It’s Pride Month, so Matt brings the queer deck and pulls The Empress: bearded, liberation-focused, shield reading live, laugh, liberate. What starts as a structure-of-the-tarot argument turns, through the card’s shadow — the great mother and the devouring mother — into the realest AI conversation we’ve had: not “is it good or evil,” but why we keep trying to shove the parts we don’t like under the rug, and what that costs us.

Matt and Jaye Anne start by arguing the architecture of the majors — is it the hero’s journey, or something else? (Matt’s read: Magician/High Priestess are the divine masculine and feminine; Empress/Emperor are the Great Mother and Great Father — more embodied, more tangible.) Then the Empress’s shadow drags the whole thing into AI: creative force and devouring force are the same force. They take apart the false-purity line, the urge to hit a “hide all AI content” button and pretend it isn’t part of reality, and the both/and they keep circling — you can’t have the light without understanding the dark. It ends, against the odds, in hope.

In this episode

* The card: The Gay Marseille Tarot (The Word Witch), the bearded Empress and the “trans masculine anarchist anti-emperor,” Audre Lorde’s erotic, and live, laugh, liberate

* Is the major arcana the hero’s journey? Divine masculine/feminine (Magician/High Priestess) vs. the Great Mother/Father (Empress/Emperor) — and the Hidden Door game Matt built so you experience the stations non-linearly

* Mariana Lewis & the archetypal tarot school; Jung, anima/animus, and why the Magician and High Priestess are ineffable, not keyword definitions

* The great mother and the devouring mother — the shadow hinge from the Empress into AI

* Fitting the narrative: how picking a side strips the nuance; the “hide all AI” button; the Anthropic / national-security export parallel; left-hand/right-hand path — “to protect yourself from a hacker, you need to know how to hack”

* Pandora’s box: the AI book cover, “TarotPulse would never have been,” and sovereignty cutting both ways

* “We don’t hide this stuff” — the unchanging evangelical God, and the Archetypal Family Field work of separating the archetype from your imago

* The devouring mother, “Your Mom’s a Bitch and It’s Okay,” Old Navy folding tables, and learning to live in the mess

* Magnets, pH, electricity, cyclical history — and the wisdom Matt gets walked into: “we’re gonna make it”

Lines that landed

* “You can be mad that we took it out of the box. That’s not going to make it go away. It’s okay to be mad — it’s just not going back in.” — Matt

* “You’re personally sovereign. You do not have to use it. You do not have to like it. But that doesn’t mean you get to tell me it is morally wrong that I did.” — Matt

* “To do the light side, you have to understand the dark side… if you want to protect yourself from a hacker, you need to know how to hack. And they’re trying to say, well that’s dark, so you can’t have the light either. What does that do? That just makes us blind.” — Matt

* “This is what mother means — its essence. But it is not the mother. It’s just an anchor we can hold on to to consider the mother through.” — Matt

* “You can’t get rid of binaries. You can get rid of the assumption that it’s an either/or. It’s both ends and everything in between. And the tension is the point.” — Matt

* “Even if all you do is your own work, you are still making things better. You don’t have to go out on a crusade to fix the world. Fix yourself.” — Matt

* “Two sides of the same coin. If you pretend the other side is over there — it’s not. You’re imagining this over there. It’s on you.” — Jaye Anne

Referenced

* The Gay Marseille Tarot by The Word Witch (thewordwitchtarot.com/gaymarseille) — the bearded Empress, the “trans masculine anarchist anti-emperor”

* Audre Lorde, “Uses of the Erotic”

* Mariana Lewis & the archetypal tarot school

* Carl Jung — anima/animus, archetypes, the imago

* The Archetypal Family Field program

* Hidden Door — Matt’s tarot-majors game with non-linear stations

* Arthur C. Clarke’s third law (callback)

* Anthropic & the national-security export restriction; export-grade browser encryption history

* Star Trek: Lower Decks — the infinite-parallel-universes rifts

* Old Navy / Aeropostale folding tables as an entropy metaphor

What we left unresolved

Where the lines actually go. They agree you have to draw some line — but every line you draw leaves something true on the other side of it. The honest version of this episode is that the answer to “what do you do with the unavoidable shadow of any creation” can be one thing this week and another next, and that drawing the line is itself the never-finished work.

Chapters

0:00 — Cold open: Toy Story, “howdy,” and the big 4-

05:44 — The card: The Empress from The Gay Marseille Tarot (Pride Month)

8:33 — Is the major arcana the hero’s journey? Divine M/F vs. Great Mother/Father

15:42 — Mariana Lewis & the archetypal tarot school

20:11 — The Empress’s shadow → AI: the great mother and the devouring mother

23:11 — Fitting the narrative: shadow/light & the “hide all AI” button

30:50 — Pandora’s box: the AI book cover, TarotPulse & sovereignty

35:18 — “We don’t hide this”: the unchanging God & separating the archetype from your imago

43:01 — The devouring mother, “Your Mom’s a Bitch and It’s Okay” & living in the mess

51:47 — The bearded Empress, “the tension is the point” & “we’re gonna make it”

~1h10 · One moment: Jaye Anne and a friend’s forever-unwritten book, “Your Mom’s a Bitch and It’s Okay.” It’s Pride Month — hence the deck. The Five of Wands does not stalk Matt this time; the Empress does.

item.title: Episode 005: There's No Waning Cycle
item.description:
Astrology isn’t predicting it; it’s reflecting it — the cosmos enforcing cycles a culture of endless progress refuses to honor. The question we couldn’t close: can you turn the heat down halfway, or does the whole thing have to burn to complete?

Two hosts who promised structure and immediately abandon it pull the Ten of Swords from the food-themed Magic Pantry deck — an onion, mid-chop, weeping — and let it drag them into the real subject: collective exhaustion in a culture that has lost its waning phase. A second pull, the Five of Wands from the Crow deck — the card that stalked them last episode — turns it toward astrology as a mirror, not a cause.

In this episode

* The card: the Magic Pantry deck (wands = spices, cups = fruit, swords = “eat your vegetables”) and the Ten of Swords as deep exhaustion

* “Long-term tired”: trauma reframed as unclosed grief tabs

* Technology has no waning cycle — iPhone to Uber to ChatGPT, zero to a million with no time to integrate

* The second pull, the recurring Five of Wands → astrology and Tarnas’s Cosmos and Psyche

* Pluto-Saturn 2020 and the Uranus-Pluto cycles of the 1960s and 2012–15

* Ole Miss across the Uranus-Pluto cycle: 1848 founding, James Meredith, the noose incident

* Astrology as reflection, not causation: “a high percentage of non-random data, we call that information”

Lines that landed

* “I’m like long-term tired.” — Jaye Anne

* “I just wanna put plants in the ground… I’m done with this chaos for the sake of chaos.” — Jaye Anne

* “I feel like we’re not ever even fully processing the cycle before the next cycle starts.” — Matt

* “There’s no waning cycle. We’re just waxing a hundred percent of the time.” — Matt

* “The planets keep moving. The universe is like, you can try, but that’s not how anything works.” — Matt

* “I don’t believe the planets cause the things. I don’t think it’s about causation. It’s way more about reflection.” — Matt

* “When we look at a significantly high percentage of non-random data, we call that information.” — Matt

Referenced

* The Magic Pantry deck & the Crow deck

* Richard Tarnas, Cosmos and Psyche

* Pluto-Saturn 2020 (COVID), the 1960s Uranus-Pluto conjunction (civil rights), the 2012–15 square

* The USA Pluto return (with Rome / Magna Carta parallels)

* Ole Miss: 1848 founding, James Meredith, the 2012–15 noose incident

* Melville & Moby-Dick

* Supabase / TarotPulse

* The iPhone, Uber, and ChatGPT growth curves

What we left unresolved

Can you dial a Ten of Swords down to a Five — turn the heat halfway — or does the over-pressurized vessel have to spark and burn to complete the cycle? “Well… that doesn’t sound great.”

Chapters

0:00 — Cold open: no plan today

1:21 — The card: Ten of Swords (the Magic Pantry deck)

10:15 — Long-term tired: trauma as unclosed grief tabs

12:18 — Technology has no waning cycle: iPhone → Uber → ChatGPT

32:52 — Second pull: the recurring Five of Wands (Crow deck)

35:00 — Cosmos and Psyche: Pluto-Saturn 2020 & the Uranus-Pluto cycles

49:19 — Ole Miss across the Uranus-Pluto cycle: 1848 → Meredith → the noose

53:45 — The US Pluto return & astrology as reflection, not causation

1:04:01 — Dial it down to a five + the hungry-podcast finale

~1h11 · One moment: Matt botching the geometry — “What is ninety plus four… I cannot do math right now. What is wrong with my brain? …Five. I can do five.” — and the cosmic-dread finale collapsing into guacamole and crostini. The Five of Wands recurs from Episode 4.

item.title: Episode 004: Animism All the Way Down
item.description:
This is the one where we mix the things you’re not supposed to mix, argue that the purity line around technology is shadow projection in an ethics costume, and follow animism past the point of comfort: if it’s animism, it’s animism all the way down, or it isn’t animism at all.

The most charged question in modern practice: can you blend AI and technology with magic, or does it make you a charlatan? Drawing the Five of Wands reversed — passionate voices pulling in five directions with no one in charge — Matt and Jaye Anne argue the loud arguments against AI are mostly shadow projection: people meeting their own fear in a mirror that reflects both the self and the collective back at them. They dismantle the false-purity line and trace technology’s mystical lineage from Mesmer through electrical healing to the Flexner Report. Their longest episode.

In this episode

* The card: the Eldritch Overload deck (Weird Works) and how to read reversals (resistance, shadow, twisting the knife)

* AI as mirror: “you’re not really mad about AI — figure out what you’re actually mad about”

* Provenance & purity policing: the sweatshop-mug thought experiment, the vaccine/abortion parallel, and “at what point am I entitled to a piece of your sovereignty?”

* Individual vs. corporate: an ADHD plastic-bag rabbit hole on why personal purity changes nothing structural

* Technology IS magic: Clarke’s law, a childhood Atari, 1980s BBS chat rooms, and a 2025 Commodore 64 next to the altar

* Animism all the way down: Crowley’s definition of magic, AI-assisted astrology against a real ephemeris

* The god of AI: “we sacrifice to the gods we create” — Mesmer, the Flexner Report, TechGnosis

Lines that landed

* “People are encountering their shadow through technology right now. AI is doing a really interesting twisting of that knife, because it is a mirror.” — Matt

* “You’re not really mad about AI. But you are mad. So figure out what you’re actually mad about.” — Matt

* “At what point am I entitled to any piece of your sovereignty? And for what reasons?” — Jaye Anne

* “If you’re gonna throw animism in my face, then it’s animism all the way down or it’s not animism.” — Matt

* “AI is not going back in the tube. That toothpaste is out.” — Matt

* “We chose science and technology as the new gods. And we sacrifice human lives to those gods every single day.” — Jaye Anne

* “Technology and magic are likely to be indistinguishable in the future. We’re making a very hair’s-line slice right now by believing we can say they’re different.” — Jaye Anne

Referenced

* The Eldritch Overload deck (Weird Works) — a tech-magic / cyberpunk deck that inverts the standard reversal meanings

* Arthur C. Clarke’s third law

* Aleister Crowley’s definition of magic

* Erik Davis, TechGnosis

* Franz Mesmer / mesmerism

* Edgar Cayce

* The Flexner Report (1910) & the AMA

* The Commodore 64 reissue, Atari 2600, Q-Link “People Connection”

* Demetra George (Hellenistic astrology)

* Zelda: Skyward Sword

What we left unresolved

What you actually do with the unavoidable harm of any creation — and the honest admission the answer can be one thing this week and something else next. “Erase the line. What value was this line to me?”

Chapters

0:00 — Cold open (music) & the howdy / y’all detour

3:33 — The card: Five of Wands reversed (the Weird Works deck)

9:06 — How to read reversals

17:10 — AI as a mirror: “you’re not really mad about AI”

22:06 — Provenance & purity: the mug, vaccines & sovereignty

32:14 — Individual vs. corporate: the plastic-bag rabbit hole

41:04 — Technology IS magic: Clarke’s law & the Commodore altar

56:02 — Animism all the way down: AI in spiritual practice

1:08:33 — The god of AI & the mystical history of tech

1:26:49 — Wind-down: predictive brains, Skyward Sword & erasing the line

~1h36 · One moment: reading the deck’s grim reversed meaning, Matt mock-panics — “What are you trying to tell us, Deck?” — then, explaining floppies to younger listeners, “a floppy disk is a 3D print of the save icon.” The Five of Wands recurs in Episode 5.

item.title: Episode 001: What Kind of Smoke Is It?
item.description:
NOTE: We forgot to pull a card.

On the debut. The one rule of the show — pull a card, follow it, leave it unresolved — missed on episode one. So we did the only honest thing a tarot-adjacent podcast can do: we pulled it late. Months later, blind, from a deck that didn’t exist when we recorded — card 32, Fumus / Smoke, from The Wild Unknown Alchemy deck. Smoldering. Warning. Illusion.

Smoke is the thing that reaches you before the fire does, and the only question it asks is what kind. Incense and herbs — or the fear-stricken scent of something burning down? That’s the whole episode: two people raised in the same smell of holiness, working out which one it was. We didn’t pull a card. The card pulled us. We just noticed late.

The debut, and the origin story under the whole show. Matt — Appalachian folk Christianity to hardcore Memphis evangelicalism (street evangelism on Beale Street) to witchcraft, across 25 years as a software architect now working in AI — and Jaye Anne — homeschooled and church-schooled six days a week, an “Irish goodbye” out by senior year — compare notes on getting free of controlling, fear-driven Christianity and what each rebuilt on the other side. Stated topic: religious trauma. Real subject: sovereignty — a spirituality that runs you versus one you author yourself.

In this episode

* Two origin stories: street-evangelist-to-witch, and the homeschool-charismatic walkout

* Charismatic vs. “stuffy” church — and the theory that the neurodivergent cluster in both

* The exits: a church schism, a “give more money” sermon the weekend of the Virginia Tech shooting, and an “atheists are sexual deviants” last straw

* The mechanism of control: how every appeal bottoms out at biblical inerrancy — which is purely circular

* Trump-era hypocrisy, end-times “fanfic from the 1800s,” and the fantasies coming true

* What’s on the other side: sovereignty, self-defined ethics, and Wisdom as a woman screaming in the streets

Lines that landed

* “I went from being an ultra-evangelical Christian to practicing witchcraft. And I’m a software engineer and architect who works professionally with AI all day, every day.” — Matt

* “Brainwashing children is part of our lifestyle. That’s exactly what it is.” — Jaye Anne

* “It’s never about actually getting people what they need. It’s about making people easier to control. If you control the ways people are allowed to hear from God, it’s not a long stretch before you can make yourself God.” — Matt

* “It’s inerrant because it says it’s inerrant.” — Matt

* “I can be so spiritual and yet retain personal sovereignty. I don’t have to have an outside authority telling me what’s okay and what’s not okay.” — Matt

Referenced

Biblical inerrancy — the circular keystone the whole structure rests on

The unforgivable sin (blasphemy of the Holy Spirit) — the undefined sin that fuels the anxiety

The Left Behind series & John Nelson Darby — the 1800s source of Rapture / end-times theology

The A Beka curriculum — "history and science from a Christian perspective"

Proverbs — "Wisdom cries out in the streets… and wisdom's a female"

The 90s Kmart "blue light special" internet

Witchcraft & the occult — the sovereign spirituality on the other side

What we left unresolved

How do you deconstruct without building a new rigid orthodoxy out of the reaction? Matt admits even the American flag is now a trigger: “and that’s probably not good either.” The exit door and the trap turn out to be the same door.

~1h20. Go deeper: “Smoke Rings,” Sam Cooke — eyes closed. To ponder: copal, sage, cedar, sandalwood.

Chapters

0:00 — Intro (cold-open music) & welcome

2:48 — Matt’s origin: evangelist to witch to AI architect

10:30 — Jaye Anne’s 90s: Kmart blue-light internet

14:54 — Charismatic vs. stuffy church & neurodivergence

22:26 — Out of the bubble: insulated worlds cracking open

27:36 — Two exits: schisms, money sermons & the last straw

37:13 — The mechanism of control: inerrancy

39:13 — Trump, hypocrisy & end-times fanfic

1:04:49 — The cost: anxiety, shame & patriotic programming

1:13:17 — After deconstruction: sovereignty & reconstruction

item.title: Episode 002: Participant, Not Consumer
item.description:
Two white people take on appropriation vs. appreciation and refuse to dodge it. The Hanged Man — Matt’s recurring card, drawn 3 of the 4 times he’s ever cut this deck — presides over the whole hour: suspension between two ways of being, willing surrender rather than giving up. The core move is to reject the clean binary: there’s no filter that spits out yes/no, and anyone selling you one is selling the colonial-purity reflex in spiritual drag. What they build instead is a working framework — participant, not consumer; reciprocity over extraction; find the through-line archetype and its local expression rather than importing the exotic object.

In this episode

* The card: the Neon Tarot, the recurring Hanged Man, and why tarot works at all (78 gateways, the tension of opposites)

* Why appropriation happens: the colonial wound, and white people severed from their own earth-connection going looking for it elsewhere

* The “appropriation police” — usually outside the tradition they’re defending — and why gatekeeping often does more harm than good

* The useful line: private practice vs. setting up as a paid teacher of a tradition you have no relationship to (Matt’s Irish pagan teacher: “you don’t get to teach this yet”)

* Inspiration, not appropriation: Weston Price, bone broth, turmeric, and finding the local instantiation of a universal archetype

* Projection and the confession: the rage is about feeling void of culture, not the practice itself

Lines that landed

* “A lot of white people are just running around trying to find something they can’t remember.” — Jaye Anne

* “Me adopting a practice and performing it in private is pretty limited in how much damage it’ll do. But when I set myself up as a teacher — and then charge you money for it — that’s when you’re in a place you probably ought not to be.” — Matt

* “Doing it in a way that is consciously trying to be in right relationship and getting it wrong is better than getting it perfect and yet having no relationship to the culture.” — Matt

* “I am going to try to be a participant in this, not a consumer of it.” — Matt

* “You can slap Christian in front of anything and it’s almost always a more disgusting version of the thing you wanted.” — Matt

* “When our answer to dealing with evil is to do evil to the evildoers… we become them.” — Matt

* “Purity is a lie. I think that’s something our brain makes up to feel safe.” — Jaye Anne

Referenced

* The Neon Tarot

* Unverified Personal Gnosis (UPG)

* Palo Santo — with mugwort and juniper as local alternatives

* Weston A. Price, Nutrition and Physical Degeneration

* Mudras & palmistry → the “Christian mudra” through-line

* “Christian yoga”

* The CreativeMind seminar — “what you believe to be real will continue to be created”

* John Donne — “no man is an island”

What we left unresolved

They refuse to answer the question on purpose. “If you thought we were gonna answer the question — we’re not, sorry.” How each person navigates right relationship is theirs alone to work out.

Chapters

0:00 — Intro (cold-open music) & welcome

1:27 — The card: Neon Tarot & the recurring Hanged Man

5:36 — What the Hanged Man means

13:57 — Why tarot works: 78 gateways to the question

16:43 — Why appropriation happens: colonialism & the culture we forgot

22:31 — The appropriation police: intuition vs. policing

28:44 — Drawing the line: participant, not consumer

46:36 — Inspiration not appropriation: the through-line archetype

53:14 — Christian-washing & the real thing

59:03 — Filtered reality, projection & the culture-void confession

1:10:07 — Purity is a lie

1:13:20 — Wrapping up: no easy answers & where to find us

~1h17 · One moment: Matt lands the pun — “we have beaten the hangman to death, which is the next card in sequence” — and at the close, “the hanged man is back. Never left.”

item.title: Episode 003: Shadow Capitalism
item.description:
On the surface, a riff on the King of Pentacles. Underneath: reality as a set of consented games — speakeasies, masks, LARPing, capitalism — and AI as an amplifier of whatever is already there, not a creator of anything new. Jaye Anne named it on-mic: “it was mostly about shadow capitalism.”

In this episode

* The card: the Gen Z Tarot’s renamed suits (Aesthetic / Mood / Facts / Guap) and the Zaddy as shadow material

* Games, rituals, masks, and reality: Robert Anton Wilson, the magic circle, speakeasies, masking and code-switching

* Capitalism as the big game — “a system that feeds on itself; you can’t optimize it without destroying it”

* AI as amplifier, not creator — the fake-pill detection app, and “AI makes good people better and bad people worse”
